I was born in Amsterdam, and I love visitors, really. But let me give you some advice. The first thing that tourists do wrong is walking in the bike lanes. Please, look before you cross. Second, the center is beautiful, but it's not the only Amsterdam. Take the free ferry behind the central station. It goes to the north, an area where you find old factories that are now restaurants and galleries. And come in the autumn. It's the season when the city is quiet, and the light on the canals in the late afternoon is something you won't forget.

My first trip to Amsterdam was in August, and honestly, I didn't love it. It was crowded, it was hot, and the lines for the museums were incredibly long. So last year I went back, in October. What a difference. The streets were calm, the trees along the canals were yellow and red, and I could walk everywhere. The highlight of the trip was a small gallery that I found by accident. It belonged to an old woman who painted the canals every day. I bought one of her paintings, and it's on my wall now. Sometimes a city needs a second chance.

On my first day in Amsterdam, I rented a bike, and I was really nervous. There were bikes everywhere, and everybody was so fast. A woman who was waiting next to me at a red light saw my face and laughed. She taught me to use my hand to show where I was turning. It helped a lot. By the third day, I was riding like a local, well, almost. On the last day, I rode out of the city, along a river, to a village where there were windmills and cows. I would never see that on foot. If you go, rent a bike. Just stay in the bike lane.
